operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10080 with a subject line describing authorizing certain Government employees to acquire a competitive civil service status. The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The one-year recommendation period (to 1950-09-30 inclusive, 1950-09-29 on the exclusive reading) is an own-terms limit on new recommendations, not shown to have ended the clause, and Executive Orders 10103 and 10535 recite the order without ending it. No earlier express end was found.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 2 of the Civil Service Act (22 
Stat. 404) and by section 1753 of the Re­
vised Statutes of the United States, it is 
hereby ordered as follows:
The incumbent in an active duty status 
of any office or position in the competitive 
service of the Federal Government on 
the date of this order who is without 
competitive status shall, upon recom­
mendation made within the period of one 
year from the date of this order by the 
head of the agency in which he is em­
ployed, acquire a competitive civil serv­
ice status if all of the following 
conditions are satisfied: (1) That such 
incumbent was appointed to an office 
or position in the executive branch of the 
Federal Government prior to March 16, 
1942 (the date on which the War Serv­
ice Regulations became effective), and 
has had continuous service with the Fed­
eral Government since that date which 
is creditable for retirement purposes, 
inclusive of any intervening military 
service; ( 2) that if the employment of 
such incumbent is evaluated under an 
efficiency rating system his most recent 
rating is “Good” or better, and if his 
employment is not evaluated under an 
efficiency rating system the head of the 
agency concerned has certified to the 
Civil Service Commission that the in­
cumbent has served with merit for six 
months or longer immediately prior to 
the date of such certification; (3) that 
such person successfully qualifies in such 
suitable noncompetitive examination as 
the Civil Service Commission may pre­
scribe; and (4) that such incumbent 
shall be given only one such noncompeti­
tive examination: Provided, that sepa­
ration for one year or less due to 
reduction of force shall not prevent the 
acquisition of a competitive status here­
under by the present incumbent in an 
active duty status of an office or position 
In the competitive service.
The Civil Service Commission shall 
promulgate regulations to effectuate the 
purposes of this order.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10080 (14 FR 5985; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10080, Enabling Certain Employees of the Federal Government To Acquire a Competitive Civil Service Status, signed September 30, 1949. Inventory: one whole-order clause with two operative sentences (an incumbent without competitive status acquires it upon an agency head's recommendation made within one year from the date of the order if four conditions are met, and the Civil Service Commission is to promulgate regulations). Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table row for 10080 describes it as authorizing certain Government employees to acquire a competitive civil service status. The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The one-year period for agency recommendations ended on 1950-09-30 on the inclusive reading (the exclusive reading, under which the period ends when that day begins, would end it on 1950-09-29); it limits new recommendations but not acquisition by a person already recommended, who must still pass a noncompetitive examination, and the order stayed on the books until express revocation. The sunset is therefore disclosed as a partial own-terms limit and not claimed as the first end of the clause. Later orders that recite 10080 are not ends: Executive Order 10103 (1950-02-01) deems certain employees of international organizations to have been in active-duty status on 1949-09-30 so far as 10080 is concerned, and Executive Order 10535 (1954-06-09) lets the Civil Service Commission confer competitive status on persons who met the requirements of 10080 or of Executive Order 10157 but were not recommended because of administrative error; neither amends 10080's text, extends its one-year period or revokes it. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

No exact date on which every recommended person had been processed is held, so the period is disclosed and not claimed as the first end. (2) Executive Order 10103 and Executive Order 10535 recite 10080 and do not revoke, supersede or extend it. (3) No other order in the held corpus cites 10080 by number. The revocation list has no saving clause; no continuing independent command of the order is shown.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number, the held table row matches its subject, and the enacting provision has no exception; it reaches the whole order. The dossier lead target provision not located: EO:10535 is resolved: Executive Order 10535 neither amends nor revokes 10080 (it creates a separate Civil Service Commission authority for administrative-error cases) and is recorded as a source note, not as a later event or end."}

savings_residuals.reason: Competitive civil service status acquired by an incumbent under the order is an accrued effect that continues independently of the order; the enacting provision of Executive Order 12553 has no savings or exception clause, and Executive Order 10535 of 1954 itself treats persons who met the order's requirements as having an entitlement to status that survived the one-year recommendation period. No held source shows acquired status being undone by revocation.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10106
C reating  a B oard o f I n q u ir y T o R eport  
on  a L abor D is p u t e A ffectin g  th e 
B itu m in o u s C oal I ndustry  o f th e 
U nited  S tates
WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute 
between certain bituminous coal operat­
ors and associations and certain of their 
employees represented by the Interna­
tional Union, United Mine Workers of 
America, involving wages and terms and 
conditions of employment; and 
WHEREAS in my opinion such dispute 
has resulted or threatens to result in a 
strike or lockout affecting a substantial 
part of the bituminous coal industry, an 
industry engaged in trade and commerce 
among the several states and with for­
eign nations, and in the production of 
goods for commerce, which strike or 
lockout, if permitted to occur or to con­
tinue, will imperil the national health 
and safety;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 206 of 
the Labor Management Relations Act, 
1947 (Public Law 101, 80th Congress), I 
hereby create a Board of Inquiry, con­
sisting of such members as I shall 
appoint, to inquire into the issues in­
volved in such dispute.
The Board shall have powers and 
duties as set forth in Title II of the said 
Act. The Board shall report to the 
President in accordance with provisions 
of section 206 of the said Act on or before 
February 13, 1950.
Upon submission of its report, the 
Board shall continue in existence to per­
form such other functions as may be 
required under the said Act, until the 
Board is terminated by the President.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10106 (15 FR 649; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10106 and signed February 6, 1950. The order creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 to inquire into the issues in a labor dispute affecting the bituminous coal industry, with a report due on a stated date and a provision that, once the report is submitted, the Board continues in existence to perform other functions required under the Act until the President terminates it. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the Board, its report date, and its continuation until terminated by the President are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10106 with a subject line matching this order (creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The report date stated in the order is a deadline for the Board, not an end. (2) The order itself provides that the Board continues until the Board is terminated by the President; a presidential termination would be an earlier express end, but no termination instrument for this Board appears in the held corpus or in the OFR catalog hits, so none is asserted. EO 12553 is itself a presidential revocation of the order by number and is the first held instrument ending it. (3) No later order amends or supersedes it in the held corpus. Evidence decides (owner ruling 2026-10-28): no earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the continuation sentence (the Board continues in existence to perform other functions under the Act until terminated by the President) is part of the same board-creating order and shares its end; the powers and duties come from Title II of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947, which the order cites and does not restate.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10112 (15 FR 1065; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10112 and signed February 24, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the Eastern Carriers' Conference Committee, the Western Carriers' Conference Committee and the Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committee and certain of their employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10112 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.

Creating  an E mergency  B oard T o I nves ­

nal  R ailroad  A ssociation  of  S t . L o u is 
and C ertain  of  I ts  E m plo y ees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Terminal Railroad Association of St. 
Louis, a carrier, and certain of its em­
ployees represented by the Brotherhood 
of Locomotive Engineers and the Broth­
erhood of Locomotive Firemen and En- 
ginemen, la,bor organizations; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions
1219
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a large section of the country 
of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate the said dispute. No member 
of the said board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Terminal Railroad Associa­
tion of St. Louis or its employees in the 
conditions out of which the said dispute 
arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10117 (15 FR 1653; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10117 and signed March 20, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the Western Carriers' Conference Committee and certain of their employees represented by the Switchmen's Union of North America, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10117 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10120, whose subject line describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute. No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. Report deadline and status-quo period are not ends; functionally spent when the board reported and the statutory period ran, but the order remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10120 (15 FR 2073; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10120 and signed April 11, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees and certain of their employees represented by the Railroad Yardmasters of America, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10120 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The machine dossier did not locate the revoking provision for this pair; the held text of EO 12553 does contain the row for this order (number followed by a subject line) in the No. Subject table on its page 10, and the enacting sentence precedes the table, so the whole held EO 12553 text is cited as the ending source. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: the held text of EO 12553 contains no savings or exception clause attached to the revocation list (the enacting provision is a single sentence followed by the table, and the only effective-date or exception wording found anywhere in the order is outside it). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10130, whose subject line describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute. No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. Report deadline and status-quo period are not ends; functionally spent when the board reported and the statutory period ran, but the order remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier express end was found.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10130
Creating an E mergency B oard T o I nves­
tigate A  Dispute  B etween  the B oston 
&  Albany R ailroad C ompany (N ew 
York C entral R. R. Company , L es­
see) and C ertain of I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Boston &  Albany Railroad Company  
(New York Central R. R. Company, 
Lessee), a carrier, and certain of its em­
ployees represented by the Brotherhood  
of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organi­
zation; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as  
to deprive a section of the country of  
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board  
of three members, to be appointed by  
me, to investigate the said dispute. No  
member of the said board shall be pecu­
niarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railway employees or any  
carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Boston &  Albany Railroad  
Company or its employees in the con­
ditions out of which the said dispute  
arose.

EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10140, whose subject line describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute. No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. EXECUTIVE ORDER 10140
Creating  an E mergency  B oard T o
I nvestigate  a D ispute  B etween  the
P ullman  C ompany  and C ertain  of I ts
Employees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Pullman Company, a carrier, and 
certain of its employees represented by 
the Order of Railway Conductors, a labor 
organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organi­
zation of railway employees or any 
carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Pullman Company or its 
employees in the conditions out of which 
the said dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10142, whose subject line describes an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute. No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. Report deadline and status-quo period are not ends; functionally spent when the board reported and the statutory period ran, but the order remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier express end was found.

Creating  a n E m ergency  B oard T o I n ­

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Braniff Airways, Inc., a carrier, and 
certain of its employees represented by 
the Brotherhood of Railway & Steamship 
Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and 
Station Employees, a labor organization; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt 
interstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate the said dispute. No member 
of the said board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Braniff Airways, Inc., or its 
employees in the conditions out of which 
the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10142 (15 FR 4465; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10142 and signed July 12, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Braniff Airways, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway & Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Employees, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10142 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The machine dossier did not locate the revoking provision for this pair; the held text of EO 12553 does contain the row for this order (number followed by a subject line) in the No. Subject table on its page 10, and the enacting sentence precedes the table, so the whole held EO 12553 text is cited as the ending source. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: the held text of EO 12553 contains no savings or exception clause attached to the revocation list (the enacting provision is a single sentence followed by the table, and the only effective-date or exception wording found anywhere in the order is outside it). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.

Creating an E mergency B oard T o I nves­
tigate a D ispute ^  Between  the N ew 
York C entral R ailroad C ompany , 
Lines  E ast of B uffalo, and C ertain 
of I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the New York Central Railroad Com­
pany, Lines East of Buffalo, a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engi­
neers, Brotherhood of Locomotive Fire­
men and Enginemen, Order of Railway 
Conductors, and Brotherhood of Rail­
road Trainmen, labor organizations; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board 
of three members, to be appointed by 
me, to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said board shall be pe­
cuniarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of railway employees or any 
carrier.

the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.

way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after thff board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the New York Central Railroad 
Company, Lines East of Buffalo, or by 
its employees, in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10147 (15 FR 5067; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10147 and signed August 4, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the New York Central Railroad Company, Lines East of Buffalo, and certain of its employees represented by four railroad labor organizations, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10147 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10165 (15 FR 6737; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10165 and signed October 3, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, Locals 808 and 459, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10165 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.

No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the American Airlines, Inc., a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the Air Line Pilots Association, In­
ternational, a labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of , the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No memi 
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
ttie President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the American Airlines, Inc., or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10203 (16 FR 385; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10203 and signed January 13, 1951. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the American Airlines, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10203 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
